title: OpenStax IA 2e Ex. 9.60: complete the square for x^2 + 6x + 5
stem_student: Rewrite f(x) = x^2 + 6x + 5 in the form f(x) = (x − h)^2 + k by completing the square. Match each algebraic step to the completed-square picture for the same function.
stem_teacher: Same licensed function as the diagram companion (mcf3m-m4-openstax-ia2e-ex960-diagram). OpenStax continues to graph by transformations; this lesson stops at the rewrite. Ontario names a(x − h)^2 + k vertex form.
answer_verification: Copied from OpenStax Intermediate Algebra 2e §9.7 Example 9.60: half of 6 is 3; 3^2 = 9; add and subtract 9; rewrite as (x + 3)^2 − 4. Page then graphs by a left-3 / down-4 shift — that graphing step is not this item.
attribution: OpenStax Intermediate Algebra 2e, §9.7 Example 9.60 (Lynn Marecek, Andrea Honeycutt Mathis). CC BY-NC-SA 4.0. https://openstax.org/books/intermediate-algebra-2e/pages/1-introduction
provenance_notes: M4-L2 bank fill 2026-09-11. Explicit completing-the-square rewrite (not the College Algebra 2e vertex-formula How To). Alternating pair with the diagram item on the same function.
